metadata.title: Claude Code and Codex Agents - Sources
metadata.description: Official documentation and current guidance for Claude Code subagents, agent teams, Codex custom agents, debate patterns, and adjacent skill authoring models

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Subagents
official_documentation.description: Canonical subagent documentation covering scopes, frontmatter fields, built-in agents, delegation behavior, fork mode, nesting, and worktree isolation. Re-verified 2026-09-02 against Claude Code 2.1.258: the model resolution order is per-invocation model -> definition frontmatter -> CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL -> main conversation (the env var came first before v2.1.251), CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 restores the override (v2.1.257+), and experimental.cacheTtl accepts 5m or 1h (v2.1.248+).

official_documentation.name: Claude Agent SDK Subagents
official_documentation.description: Programmatic subagent definition via AgentDefinition; package names, allowedTools requirements, and runtime constraints. Re-verified 2026-08-27: recursive spawn defaults to three layers; interactive fork mode runs Claude-spawned subagents in the background and removes the run_in_background parameter.

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Agent Teams
official_documentation.description: When to use experimental collaborative agent teams instead of focused subagents, including peer messaging, shared tasks, display modes, limitations, and teammate definition reuse. Re-verified 2026-09-02: teammate model order, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE applying to teammates, and subagentPromptCacheTtl: 1h for the out-of-bucket five-minute teammate cache.

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Codex Models
official_documentation.description: Codex model catalog. Verified 2026-09-07: Astra is the most capable model for complex work; Sol suits complex open-ended work, Terra everyday work, and Luna clear repeatable tasks. The user-selected policy uses Astra low for critical roles, Sol medium as the standard fallback (changed from Luna max on 2026-09-25 to match the deployed Codex config), and Luna low for explicitly mechanical roles; this is a deployment choice, not a measured optimum.

community_resources.name: cursor pstack plugin (MIT)
community_resources.description: MIT-licensed external plugin. Accessed 2026-09-29. Informed the delegate-result-hygiene rule (drop/rerun on missing commit-or-tree-state and method; never resume an interrupted worker with changed scope), the qa-test-reviewer vacuous-test pre-check, and the hill-climbing loop guardrails (one change per measurement, freeze a sensitivity-verified harness, stop on stated target plus minimum attempts, decision logging). Rules adapted and rewritten in this repository's own words; no text copied verbatim.

research_2025_2026.name: MAST: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
research_2025_2026.description: Cemri, Pan, Yang et al., NeurIPS 2025. Canonical taxonomy of 14 multi-agent failure modes across 3 categories: specification (44.0%), inter-agent misalignment (32.15%), task verification (23.85%) per v3 (Oct 2025) Figure 1 over 1,642 traces, κ=0.88; earlier versions quote other splits. Cross-referenced in references/mast-failure-taxonomy.md.

research_2025_2026.name: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
research_2025_2026.description: Documents systematic cases where multi-agent debate degrades performance below single-agent baselines, especially under correlated base models, weak+strong agent mixing, and sycophancy bias. Source for the 'When NOT to Debate' anti-trigger table.

research_2025_2026.name: Persuasion-Driven Adversarial Influence in Multi-Agent LLM Debate
research_2025_2026.description: Nature Sci Reports 2026. Shows weak agents can persuade stronger agents off correct answers; quantifies sycophancy hazard in mixed-capability teams.

research_2025_2026.name: Adaptive Stability Detection for Multi-Agent Debate
research_2025_2026.description: OpenReview 2026. Beta-Binomial mixture + Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for non-numeric debate convergence detection. Source for the adaptive stopping rule in debate-quickstart.md.

research_2025_2026.name: HiveMind: Contribution-Guided Online Prompt Optimization
research_2025_2026.description: Dec 2025. Online per-member prompt mutation guided by Shapley contribution. Source for team-theory mechanism #17 (online Shapley-driven prompt evolution).

research_2025_2026.name: Shapley-Coop: Credit Assignment for Emergent Cooperation
research_2025_2026.description: OpenReview 2025. Shapley Chain-of-Thought reasoning + structured negotiation for spontaneous cooperation via task-time pricing. Cited in mechanism #17 (HiveMind / online Shapley prompt evolution).

research_2025_2026.name: From Debate to Equilibrium (ECON, full paper)
research_2025_2026.description: OpenReview ICML 2025 record for ECON Bayesian Nash Equilibrium coordination. Primary reference for mechanism #1.

research_2025_2026.name: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems Taxonomy
research_2025_2026.description: 2025. Names holonic and nested-summary topology patterns. Source for the Industry Vocabulary section in subagents-vs-teams-architecture.md.

research_2025_2026.name: Conductor vs Swarm: Multi-Agent AI Architecture Guide 2026
research_2025_2026.description: 2026 industry vocabulary mapping for centralized (Conductor) vs decentralized (Swarm) vs hybrid topology. Used to align this skill's internal terminology with current industry naming.

research_2025_2026.name: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA)
research_2025_2026.description: Together AI 2024. Layered proposer/aggregator topology where N agents fan out on the same prompt and an aggregator merges. Source for the MoA harness pattern in harness-patterns.md and the MoA-layered topology row in subagents-vs-teams-architecture.md.

research_2025_2026.name: Self-MoA
research_2025_2026.description: 2025. Demonstrates that on verifiable tasks, a single strong model sampled N times + aggregator beats heterogeneous MoA. Source for the Self-MoA Conditional in mechanism #2 (adversarial debate) and the Self-MoA variant in harness-patterns.md.

research_2025_2026.name: Beyond Majority Voting (BMV)
research_2025_2026.description: 2025. Optimal Weight (confidence × calibration) + Inverse Surprising Popularity recovers minority-correct answers from best-of-N. Source for game-theory mechanism #18.

research_2025_2026.name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
research_2025_2026.description: Anthropic 2022. Foundational paper for self-critique against an explicit principles list. Source for the Constitutional decision mask (mask #7).

research_2025_2026.name: Efficient Majority-then-Stopping (EMS)
research_2025_2026.description: 2026. Hoeffding-style bound: stop when leader has > N/2 + sqrt(N) votes — further sampling cannot flip the outcome. Source for the EMS stopping rule in debate-quickstart.md.

research_2025_2026.name: Radial Consensus Score (RCS)
research_2025_2026.description: 2026. Embedding-centroid best-of-N selector for semantically clustered but lexically diverse answers. Source for game-theory mechanism #19.

research_2025_2026.name: From Debate to Decision: Conformal Social Choice for Safe Multi-Agent Deliberation
research_2025_2026.description: Apr 2026. Calibrated act-vs-escalate decision layer for multi-agent debate outputs. Source for game-theory mechanism #20.

research_2025_2026.name: The Provenance Paradox in Multi-Agent LLM Routing
research_2025_2026.description: Mar 2026. Delegation contracts and attested identity for routing across trust boundaries. Source for game-theory mechanism #21.

research_2025_2026.name: Coalition Formation in LLM Agent Networks
research_2025_2026.description: Apr 2026. Hedonic-game coalition formation and stable partitions for LLM agent networks. Source for team-theory mechanism #22.

research_2025_2026.name: Mapping Human Anti-Collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems
research_2025_2026.description: Apr 2026. Anti-collusion controls for multi-agent AI systems; informs adversarial routing, reputation, and act/escalate safeguards.

research_2025_2026.name: Multi-Agent Teams Hold Experts Back (Pappu et al., Stanford)
research_2025_2026.description: Feb 2026 preprint, NOT peer-reviewed. Self-organizing LLM teams underperform best member via RLHF-agreeableness overcompromising (Expert-Leveraging Gap); abstract reports 'performance losses of up to 41.1% on ML benchmarks'. Basis for 'single strong agent beats a team' gate.

research_2025_2026.name: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets (Tran & Kiela)
research_2025_2026.description: Apr 2026 preprint, NOT peer-reviewed; scope text-only multi-hop reasoning. DPI argument for single-agent superiority at equal budget. Basis for Token-Budget Equivalence Rule. Verify before relying.

research_2025_2026.name: Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies (MASS)
research_2025_2026.description: Google DeepMind + Cambridge, ICLR 2026 (peer-reviewed). Prompt and topology are jointly optimizable; local prompt -> topology -> global prompt search order. Basis for the prompt-topology co-optimization note.

research_2025_2026.name: OX Security — Systemic MCP STDIO RCE advisory (CVE-2026-30623)
research_2025_2026.description: April 2026, multi-source corroborated + CVE. By-design config->OS-command execution in official MCP SDK stdio; Anthropic declined a protocol fix. Basis for the mcpServers stdio safe-default.

research_2025_2026.name: Team Topologies, 2nd Edition - Afterword on AI agent fleets
research_2025_2026.description: Skelton and Pais (IT Revolution, 2025). Afterword applies human team-boundary thinking to groups of AI agents: clear domain boundaries, constrained operating context, explainable decisions, audit trails, telemetry, stewardship, and avoiding handoffs between agent groups. Their small-language-model claim is an unevidenced 2025 prediction, recorded as a hypothesis to pressure-test in references/team-design-rationale.md, not a design rule.
